card.name: Old-style encyclopedic prose, noun after adjective
card.fires_on: Words in the middle of formal, dated history or encyclopedia-style prose, often a noun or word ending right after a descriptive adjective. Examples are 'vegetation', 'doctrine' and 'shirt'.

modes.label: Noun after adjective
modes.description: A noun completing a phrase with a descriptive or proper adjective in historical prose.

modes.label: Ending of an -ism word
modes.description: The ending of an abstract word like specialism or mysticism in intellectual history.
modes.example: the more speculative pantheistic myst<<icism>> of John Scotus Eriugena

modes.label: Linking word in a clause
modes.description: A small verb or preposition inside a historical sentence.
modes.example: Ideas of political autonomy<< were>> beginning to take definite shape.
